newsitem.title: UK: Kenya urges cautious E Africa economy cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Kenya urges cautious E Africa economy cooperation.

text.p: Kenya's finance minister on Thursday warned that moves to increase economic cooperation in East Africa must proceed with caution.

"It would be ridiculous if we were to implement policy projects and then we were seen to be reversing them," Musalia Mudavadi told a news conference after meeting ministers from Uganda and Tanzania in London.

Mudavadi had been asked whether the East African Cooperation project launched in March in the region could eventually result in the three countries adopting a common currency along the lines of the single currency planned by the European Union.
"I think the long-term objective can be extremely wide," he said, "but we want to tackle it carefully and cautiously."
"We must be sure that our economies are running basically on policies that we can all understand, on policies which are not impacting negatively on another country, before we get to that level."
Mudavadi was backed by Francis Muthaura, executive secretary of the Commission for East African Cooperation, who said convertibility of the three countries' currencies was already in place.
"We are satisfied with convertibility. It is a natural evolution that we are going to follow," he said.

Ugandan finance minister Mayanja Nkangi said the three countries, which until 1977 formed the East African Community, aimed to harmonise budgets and tax rates and should have dismantled tariff barriers within three or four years.
The three partners also aim to cooperate in developing the infrastructure of the region via improved telecommunications, better roads and more efficient power generation and oil pipelines.
